questions.question: During acceleration, what happens to a sidecar attached to a motorcycle?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates uncontrollably.
It makes acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to the side of your motorcycle. Because of inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply firm, smooth pressure and gradually increase the force.

questions.question: When riding in a group through a curve, how should motorcycles be arranged?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
Side by side.
Using both lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, groups ride in a staggered formation. However, move into a single-file line when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets interfere with steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration while protecting you. Modern jackets are designed to protect riders against overheating, even in warm weather.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?

options.text: The helmet meets DOT standards.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Wearing a good leather jacket.
Wearing sturdy boots.
Knowing motorcycle laws well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best defense against hitting other vehicles is to stay far away from them. Leave plenty of space so you have time to react to other drivers' mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the middle of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who move into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of the lane.
questions.explanation: When you want to prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze into your lane, ride in the middle of the lane.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: In the middle of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.
Your position in the lane does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the middle of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance does a motorcycle need compared to a car?

options.text: Much less distance.
Less distance.
The same distance.
More distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of rules, such as speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: If the rear tire locks on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Release and apply the rear brake again.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You will still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: The passing vehicle may move back into your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is safer.
You may feel a strong wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they will not have to rush to keep up with the group. More experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They rarely need to be replaced.
They scratch and become brittle and need regular replacement.
They should break easily in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They scratch and become brittle and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are plastic and will scratch and become brittle over time. Replace them regularly for the best protection.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for the best grip. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: Is the oily strip in the center of a lane safe for motorcycles?

options.text: No, it is never safe for motorcycles.
Yes, it is safe unless the road is wet.
No, you should always avoid it.
Yes, it improves traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from car drippings collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area still has enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with what color lettering?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do at night since it is hard for other drivers to see motorcycles?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Honk the horn repeatedly.
Do not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Ride safely at night by slowing down, increasing your following distance, using the headlights of cars ahead to see farther, using your high beam (unless near other vehicles), and being flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars need about the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes it especially hard for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Get maximum braking power by fully applying both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: You may not need a larger space between you and the car ahead if:

options.text: The road is slippery.
You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
The weather and traffic are good.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather and traffic are good.
questions.explanation: Keep a larger space between your vehicle and the one ahead during poor conditions. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothes to protect against cold.
Ride for more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to protect against cold.
questions.explanation: Wear clothes that protect you from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take breaks every 2 hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants—they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobbling?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Improper loading
Wrong accessories
Uneven road

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: Swerving on a motorcycle:

options.text: Needs a lot of traction.
Needs little traction.
Is a slow move.
Should be done to avoid hazards on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needs a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be done safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery roads.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect against weather discomforts like heat and cold.
